extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting manuscripts to American Sociological Review (ASR)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for authors revising manuscripts for possible acceptance at the American Sociological Review, including production-stage obligations, content/clarity expectations, and submission/ethics procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective revisions addressing reviewers' concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: The revisions that you made to the manuscript are very effective in addressing the remaining concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors signal acceptance when revisions effectively address remaining concerns. In the conditional acceptance letter, authors are asked to carefully consider and implement reviewers' detailed comments to improve the manuscript's effectiveness and create a manuscript with "maximum punch."

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyedit proof stage is crucial (final opportunity for corrections)
rubrics_metrics.description: The copyedit proof stage is crucial. It is the only opportunity for the author(s) to make necessary corrections to the text of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you receive your copyedit proof, check it thoroughly. Significant changes after this stage are not possible and even minor changes are difficult given the production schedule. The copyedit proofs are sent as MS Word attachments; after copyediting the article is typeset and a PDF proof is emailed for proofreading/layout approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors will make editorial changes to increase accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: We will be making some editorial changes ourselves to make the article more accessible, and you will have such edits to review at the copyediting stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should expect editorial edits aimed at accessibility and will be asked to review those edits during copyediting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript accessibility to a wide readership
rubrics_metrics.description: All ASR manuscripts be accessible to as much of the potential readership as possible – the vast majority of those with sociology PhDs from research universities should be able to understand why the issue is important, what the argument is, and what the findings are.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Achieve accessibility in the abstract, introduction, and conclusions and throughout the manuscript. Translate subdisciplinary jargon into ordinary English so readers outside the subdiscipline can understand and benefit from the article. Put yourself in the shoes of a wide readership and eventual graduate-seminar readings packets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript length constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Please be mindful of the manuscript's length (approximately 12,837 words) when making revisions. The next draft should be no longer than 13,000 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any additions should be significantly offset by tightening the prose elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific response to reviewers when submitting revision
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting your revised manuscript, you will be able to respond to the comments made by the reviewer(s) in the space provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this space to document any changes you make to the original manuscript and be as specific as possible in your response to the reviewer(s) to expedite processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide methodological detail: categories, coding, inter-coder reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond to calls for information on categories and coding, and inter-coder reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement reviewers' requests for additional methodological information (e.g., coding schemes, inter-coder reliability measures) to strengthen transparency and credibility of the analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify key concepts and enrich thematic analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify conceptual terms (e.g., 'dualism' and 'tragic') and consider enriching analysis by systematically highlighting themes such as 'temporality' and 'spatiality.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address reviewers' requests for conceptual clarification and consider expanding analytic framing where suggested to improve interpretive depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness and vetting of analysis; address counterarguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure the analysis is sound, thoroughly vetted, and considers (without belaboring) the significant counter arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure analytic robustness and acknowledge or refute significant counterarguments concisely to increase confidence for a broad readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage sharing supplemental materials for replication
rubrics_metrics.description: To encourage replication and validation of published research, consider adding a footnote offering access to the data, coding syntax, statistical commands, or selected narrative materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may post supplemental materials on their own website or ASR's 'Supplemental Materials' website to facilitate replication and validation of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics: do not submit elsewhere while under review; disclose prior publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of the manuscript to another professional journal while it is under review by ASR is regarded by the ASA as unethical, and significant findings or contributions that have already appeared (or will appear) elsewhere must be clearly identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are required to abide by ASA guidelines and ethics codes; the editors assume the manuscript is not under review elsewhere and that portions have not been published elsewhere in whole or in part. Notify editors if that is not true.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow ScholarOne revision submission procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise your manuscript using a word processing program and upload the revised manuscript through your Author Center (Create a Revision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You will be unable to make revisions on the originally submitted version. A link may be provided to start the revision process without logging in. Delete redundant files before completing the submission. Your manuscript number is appended to denote a revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production-stage proofreading and layout approval
rubrics_metrics.description: After the copyedit proof stage, the article is typeset and a PDF proof is e-mailed to the corresponding author for proofreading and for approval of the layout of tables and/or figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should carefully proofread the typeset PDF and approve table/figure layouts; the earlier copyedit stage remains the main opportunity for text corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to engage in outreach (optional podcast)
rubrics_metrics.description: ASR invites authors to collaborate with Sage Publications to produce an audio podcast for your paper; participation is entirely voluntary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Podcasts will appear on the ASR website and can help reach audiences such as students. Editors or Sage staff will contact authors to schedule a short call to discuss the research for the podcast.
